title: "6 · Do RFAs produce different science than parent PAs?"
subtitle: "A confounded raw comparison, corrected with a controlled regression"
format:
  html:

jupyter: python3
---

NIH funds research through different **funding opportunity** types: broad parent
**Program Announcements (PA)**, and targeted **Requests for Applications (RFA)**
that set aside money for a defined priority. A natural question (and an Open
Mike–style one): does the *type* of opportunity relate to research output?

This notebook shows why the **raw** comparison is misleading, and uses a
controlled regression over the full ExPORTER bulk data to get an adjusted
answer. Requires the bulk DuckDB store (`nih-agent bulk build` + `build-pubs`).

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from nih_science_agent.storage import duckdb_store
```

## The grant-level panel

One row per grant: funding, mechanism (activity code), fiscal year, FOA type,
and lifetime distinct linked publications — straight from DuckDB.

```{python}
con = duckdb_store.connect()
df = duckdb_store.grant_level_panel(
    con, ic="NCI", years=list(range(2006, 2011)), funding_floor=100_000
).df()
con.close()

df = df[df.foa_type.isin(["RFA", "PA", "PAR", "NONE"])].copy()
# keep mechanisms with enough grants so the dummy variables are well-estimated
keep = df.activity_code.value_counts()
df = df[df.activity_code.isin(keep[keep >= 30].index)]
df["log_funding"] = np.log(df.funding)
df["log_pubs"] = np.log1p(df.pubs)
print(f"{len(df):,} grants · {df.activity_code.nunique()} mechanisms · FY2006–2010 · NCI")
```

## The naïve picture (confounded)

```{python}
df.groupby("foa_type").agg(
    grants=("pubs", "size"),
    mean_funding=("funding", "mean"),
    mean_pubs=("pubs", "mean"),
).round(0)
```

Taken at face value, **RFA grants look the most productive** (highest mean pubs).
But RFAs also fund **larger grants and different mechanisms** — so this compares
apples to oranges. More money and bigger mechanisms buy more publications
regardless of opportunity type.

## The controlled regression

Model `log(1 + publications)` on FOA type, **holding mechanism, fiscal year, and
(log) funding constant**. PA is the reference category.

```{python}
model = smf.ols(
    "log_pubs ~ C(foa_type, Treatment('PA')) + log_funding "
    "+ C(activity_code) + C(fiscal_year)",
    data=df,
).fit()

eff = []
for name in model.params.index:
    if "foa_type" in name:
        coef, p = model.params[name], model.pvalues[name]
        lo, hi = model.conf_int().loc[name]
        eff.append({
            "vs_PA": name.split("T.")[1][:-1],
            "pct_diff": round((np.exp(coef) - 1) * 100),
            "ci_low_%": round((np.exp(lo) - 1) * 100),
            "ci_high_%": round((np.exp(hi) - 1) * 100),
            "p": f"{p:.1e}",
        })
print(f"R² = {model.rsquared:.2f}, n = {int(model.nobs):,}")
pd.DataFrame(eff)
```

The sign **flips**: adjusted for mechanism, year, and funding, **RFA-funded
grants produce ~30–35% *fewer* publications than parent-PA grants** (highly
significant). The raw advantage was entirely a confound — RFAs win on absolute
output only because they fund bigger grants.

```{python}
# forest plot of the adjusted FOA effects (% vs PA, 95% CI)
e = pd.DataFrame(eff).set_index("vs_PA")
ax = e["pct_diff"].plot.barh(xerr=[e.pct_diff - e["ci_low_%"], e["ci_high_%"] - e.pct_diff],
                             color="steelblue", title="Publications vs parent PA (adjusted, %)")
ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.8); ax.set_xlabel("% difference in publications vs PA")
```

## What this does and does not say

**Does** say: net of mechanism, year, and dollars, grants funded through RFAs are
associated with fewer *linked publications* than parent-PA grants in this NCI
2006–2010 cohort.

**Does not** say *why*, and should not be read as "RFAs are wasteful":

- **Publications are a narrow output.** RFAs often target outcomes pubs don't
  capture — cohorts, datasets, methods, trials, translation. (Pair this with the
  trial/dataset/`pulse` analyses.)
- **Unmodeled selection.** RFAs fund *targeted, often higher-risk or newer* areas;
  the model controls for mechanism and dollars but not topic, PI track record, or
  grant intent.
- **Linkage is authoritative-only** (RePORTER pub lists undercount) and **lifetime
  pubs are right-censored** for newer grants (mitigated here by fixed-year dummies
  and an older cohort).

The value of the exercise is methodological: the controlled estimate **reverses**
the headline you'd get from the raw means — exactly the kind of correction the
"knowledge creation at NIH" framing argues every funding metric needs.
